defects.severity: medium (memory safety; reachable only after allocator refusal, but the module itself defines that state as safe)
defects.description: BIO_ssl_shutdown read (*bdata).ssl without checking that the BIO's data slot was non-NULL. A refused BIO_C_SET_SSL re-creation deliberately leaves BIO.ptr NULL and init 0 ('poisoned but safe'); a later BIO_ssl_shutdown on that live chain dereferenced NULL. The pinned authorities (3.0.22/3.5.9/4.0.2 bio_ssl.c) guard bdata != NULL.
defects.fix: Wrap the ssl read and SSL_shutdown call in an if !bdata.is_null() guard, matching the authority.
defects.divergence: None; the guard is the authority's own behaviour.

defects.class: NULL data-slot dereference (authority UB not reproduced)
defects.description: BIO_ssl_copy_session_id found an SSL BIO by method type and dereferenced its data slot without a NULL check. The authority has the same unconditional dereference; AGENTS.md section 17 forbids reproducing a C-authority UB mechanism.
defects.fix: Refuse (return 0) when either located BIO has a NULL data slot. No ownership or ABI change.
defects.divergence: Recorded deliberate safety improvement: the authority would dereference NULL; the converted implementation refuses.

defects.class: transcribed ownership transfer loss (AGENTS.md section 8 compatibility axis)
defects.description: In the BIO_C_SET_SSL recovery arm (data slot NULL because an earlier re-creation failed), ssl_new installed a fresh block but the function never assigned the caller's SSL * to it. The authority always executes bs->ssl = (SSL *)ptr, so the caller's connection is adopted and released by the BIO; here it was neither adopted nor released, and the BIO remained with a NULL connection.
defects.fix: Assign ssl = ptr as *mut Ssl after the successful ssl_new, before the common BIO_set_shutdown/bs->ssl store.
